title: The Eiffel Tower Is Taller in Summer Than in Winter

scenes.text: The Eiffel Tower is taller in summer than in winter.
Between the coldest winter day and the hottest summer day, the tower stretches by about fifteen centimetres.
And it moves sideways too. The sun warms only one side, so the top leans away from it, tracing a circle about fifteen centimetres wide over a clear day.
Nobody is touching it. Thousands of tonnes of iron are quietly changing shape above the tourists every single day.
It happens because of thermal expansion. Heat makes the atoms in metal jiggle harder and take up more room, and three hundred metres of iron adds up.
Bridges and railway tracks have gaps built in for the same reason. Which landmark should I measure next?

description:
The Eiffel Tower is taller in summer than in winter.
Between the coldest and hottest days of the year, the iron tower expands and contracts by about 15 centimetres. Because the sun heats only one side, the top also leans away from the sun, drifting in a circle roughly 15 centimetres across over a sunny day.
The cause is thermal expansion: heat makes the metal take up more room, and 300 metres of iron adds up.
Which landmark should I measure next?
